sent_bad: **Children's books** tend to struggle with self-publishing, since many self-published books are e-books only, few children have e-readers, and adults (parents, grandparents) buy physical gifts and worry about screen time.

It says it "can be difficult to know whether it's financially better to shop around your manuscript a little longer, waiting for that big advance, or whether you should go ahead and self-publish to start selling copies now," and that the answer depends on your genre and target age group.

The only concrete profit figures it gives are the traditional advance range ($1,000–$2,000 up to six figures or more, before the agent's ~15% cut), while self-publishing income is entirely sales-driven with no advance but possible up-front costs.
